result: The authors developed three conditional CCT gene targeting strategies (GFP RNA interference, Flp-out, and CRISPR/Cas9) and validated their effectiveness through immunofluorescent imaging and behavioral assays. Pan-neuronal expression of shRNAGFP or flipase almost completely eliminated GFP signals, and ablation of nAChRα2 mirrored the knockout phenotype. However, some cCCT knockin flies showed lethality similar to their mutants, and leaky expression was observed in some control conditions.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledged the creation and validation of the conditional genetic tools as a major contribution. Reviewer 2 stated the authors 'provide clear evidence of the effectiveness of the new methods along with a transparent assessment of the variability of the tools,' and Reviewer 3 noted 'the generation/characterization of new tools for conditional targeting' as a strength. The reviewers accepted the validation data showing high efficiency of the approaches.

result: The authors developed CRISPR/Cas9-based conditional knockout (C-cCCTomics) using optimized sgRNA scaffolds targeting CCT genes. Cas9.HC/sgRNA eliminated most GFP signals and phenocopied known mutants (Pdfr knockout), but showed incomplete efficiency for some genes (e.g., Dh31) and failed to produce expected sleep phenotypes for nAChRα2.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the CRISPR/Cas9 approach as effective but with variable efficiency. Reviewer 2 noted 'concerns about the variability of knockout effectiveness' but acknowledged the 'transparent assessment of the variability of the tools.' Reviewer 1 stated the paper is 'convincing to show that the tools indeed allow to efficiently and specifically eliminate neuropeptides/receptors from subsets of neurons,' accepting the data despite incomplete efficiency for some targets.

result: The authors engineered improved Cas9 variants (Cas9.M6 and Cas9.M9) by fusing chromatin-modulating peptides (HMGN1 and HMGB1) to enhance gene knockout efficiency. Cas9.M9 achieved 97.19% knockout efficiency for ple compared to 69.58% for Cas9.HC, with average efficiencies of ~90% across multiple genes. These variants showed higher mutagenesis rates and successfully phenocopied mutants in behavioral assays.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the improved Cas9 variants as a significant technical advance. Reviewer 3 specifically highlighted 'the design and testing of improved versions of Cas9 for efficient knock out' as a strength. Reviewer 2 acknowledged the authors 'provide clear evidence of the effectiveness of the new methods,' and no concerns were raised about the Cas9 variant data. The quantitative efficiency improvements and behavioral validation were not questioned.

result: Using Flp-out and split-LexA intersection strategies, the authors identified 43 CCT genes expressed in circadian neurons across eight subsets. They confirmed known expression patterns (CCHa1, sNFP, Trissin) and identified new ones (nAChRα1, nAChRα2, GABA-B-R2 in LNvs). Some findings showed broader expression than previously reported (Nplp1, Dh31), and Pdf/Pdfr showed no stable signals in Flp-out experiments despite known expression.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged the expression profiling but raised concerns about accuracy. Reviewer 2 noted 'concerns about...the accuracy of the gene expression approach' and that the profiling is 'complementary to the ones already published,' suggesting it adds information but may have limitations. Reviewer 1 stated the results 'appear to depend on CNMA_expressing DN1ps' without questioning the expression data directly, but the discrepancies with known Pdf/Pdfr expression and broader labeling patterns indicate methodological limitations that reviewers implicitly recognized.

result: The authors conducted a pilot screen of CCT gene knockouts in clock neurons, reproducing known phenotypes (Pdf, Pdfr, Dh31) and identifying CNMa as having the highest MAPI value. However, leaky expression of Cas9.M9 and sgRNA caused unintended disruption of some genes (Dh31, Dh44, Pdf, Pdfr), limiting the suitability of this approach for certain genes.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the pilot screen results and the identification of CNMa. Reviewer 1 noted 'the analysis of the CNMa function in the clock network reveals a new and interesting function,' and Reviewer 3 stated the authors 'uncovered a role for CNMamide...in the timing of morning anticipation.' The leaky expression issue was acknowledged by Reviewer 2 as part of the 'transparent assessment of the variability of the tools,' indicating acceptance of both the findings and their limitations.

result: Conditional knockout of CNMa in clock neurons advanced morning activity and increased MAPI in both sexes, with CNMa knockout flies phenocopying the conditional knockout. CNMa is expressed in DN1p neurons (four DN1p and one DN3), with two type I neurons showing anterior projections being the main functional subset regulating morning anticipation, as type I-specific knockout showed advanced morning peak while type II-specific knockout did not.
evaluation: Reviewers fully accepted the CNMa findings as a novel discovery. Reviewer 1 stated 'the analysis of the CNMa function in the clock network reveals a new and interesting function for CNMa in the control of morning anticipation in LD conditions' and that 'this function appears to depend on CNMA_expressing DN1ps.' Reviewer 3 noted the authors 'uncovered a function for the CNMa neuropeptide...that contributes to the temporal organization of locomotor activity.' No concerns were raised about the CNMa data or conclusions.

result: Two Pdfr and CNMa double-positive DN1ps with type I projection patterns were identified. Pdfr reintroduction in type I CNMa neurons (GMR51H05, GMR79A11) partially rescued Pdfr knockout phenotypes more effectively than type II neurons (GMR91F02). Pdfr knockout in type I CNMa neurons decreased morning anticipation, suggesting CNMa secretion may be regulated by PDF/PDFR signaling.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the relationship between CNMa and PDF/PDFR signaling. Reviewer 2 noted 'the issue regarding opposing effects of PDF signaling and CNMa, which was also raised by Reviewer One still stands, notwithstanding the edits made to the text.' This indicates that while the data on Pdfr-CNMa interactions were presented, the interpretation of their relationship and the speculation about CNMa secretion regulation remained problematic or unclear to reviewers.

result: CNMaR knockout (CNMaRKO-p65AD) showed advanced morning activity and increased MAPI in both sexes, similar to CNMa knockout. CNMaR is expressed broadly across the brain (DN1p, DN3, PI, SOG) with projections to multiple regions. Conditional knockout of CNMaR in neurons phenocopied the CNMaR knockout, indicating CNMaR functions similarly to CNMa in regulating morning anticipation.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the CNMaR findings as supporting the CNMa story. Reviewer 1 stated 'the results indicate that CNMA acts from a subset of DN1ps...with an advanced morning activity in the absence of the neuropeptide' and noted 'the receptor for the PDF neuropeptide appears to be acting in some of the CNMa neurons,' acknowledging the receptor data. No specific concerns were raised about the CNMaR knockout or expression data, indicating acceptance of these findings as part of the overall CNMa/CNMaR story.

result: Loss of CNMa in DN1ps or CNMaR causes advanced morning activity, indicating a suppressive role of CNMa-CNMaR on morning anticipation, opposite to the promoting role of PDF-PDFR. This establishes an antagonistic relationship between CNMa-CNMaR and PDF-PDFR signaling in regulating morning anticipation.
evaluation: Reviewers questioned the antagonistic relationship claim. Reviewer 2 explicitly stated 'the issue regarding opposing effects of PDF signaling and CNMa, which was also raised by Reviewer One still stands, notwithstanding the edits made to the text.' This indicates that while the advanced morning activity phenotype was accepted, the interpretation of an antagonistic relationship between CNMa-CNMaR and PDF-PDFR remained problematic. The reviewers did not reject the data but questioned the mechanistic interpretation.
